evidence.title: State of the Art and Future Perspectives in Advanced CMOS Technology.
evidence.abstract: The international technology roadmap of semiconductors (ITRS) is approaching the historical end point and we observe that the semiconductor industry is driving complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) further towards unknown zones. Today's transistors with 3D structure and integrated advanced strain engineering differ radically from the original planar 2D ones due to the scaling down of the gate and source/drain regions according to Moore's law. This article presents a review of new architectures, simulation methods, and process technology for nano-scale transistors on the approach to the end of ITRS technology. The discussions cover innovative methods, challenges and difficulties in device processing, as well as new metrology techniques that may appear in the near future.

mechanism_map.mechanism: Integrated advanced strain engineering to manipulate dislocation structures at grain boundaries
mechanism_map.intervention: Apply a controlled thermal‑mechanical treatment to the borosilicate glass liner that induces compressive surface strain and refines grain‑boundary dislocation networks, thereby limiting grain‑boundary sliding
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Reduced grain‑boundary sliding at elevated temperatures, allowing higher service temperature while maintaining structural integrity of the liner
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Conduct comparative high‑temperature creep/creep‑rupture tests on treated versus untreated liners, measuring the temperature at which grain‑boundary sliding initiates and the associated strain rates
